title: 🌍 UNIT 2: CLIMATE CLASSIFICATION AND CLIMATE REGIONS OF OUR WORLD
notes: Climate varies from place to place, but areas with similar climatic patterns can be grouped into climatic regions.

title: 🌡️ 2.1 CRITERIA FOR CLIMATE CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Climate classification :- systematic grouping of areas according to similarities in climatic conditions.

It helps to :-
🔹 Identify climatic similarities and differences.
🔹 Predict expected weather patterns.
🔹 Compare climatic conditions between regions.
🔹 Understand climate variability and change.

Common data used :- temperature, precipitation, natural vegetation and soil.

⭐ Two major approaches :-
1️⃣ Genetic classification
2️⃣ Empirical classification

title: 🏛️ 2.1.1 ANCIENT GREEK CLIMATE CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Ancient Greeks classified climates mainly according to latitude, temperature, sunlight and perceived habitability.

🔥 Torrid Zone :- hot tropical region.

🌤️ Temperate Zone :- region between the Torrid and Frigid zones; considered relatively suitable for human habitation.

❄️ Frigid Zone :- very cold polar regions around the Arctic and Antarctic circles.

⭐ Foundation :- Earth-Sun relationship and distribution of solar energy.

title: 🧬 2.1.2 GENETIC CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Genetic classification :- classifies climate according to the processes or causes that produce it.

Main factors considered :-
🔹 Air masses
🔹 Atmospheric circulation
🔹 Fronts
🔹 Jet streams
🔹 Solar radiation
🔹 Topography

✅ Advantage :- scientifically explains the causes of climate.

⚠️ Limitation :- more complex to apply because it requires detailed atmospheric information.

title: 📊 2.1.3 EMPIRICAL CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Empirical classification :- uses observed climatic data and defined limits to classify climates.

Common data :-
🌡️ Temperature
🌧️ Precipitation
🌿 Vegetation

Examples :- Köppen and Trewartha systems.

✅ Advantage :- relatively simple when reliable climatic data are available.

⭐ Similar climatic characteristics are grouped into the same climate type.

title: 🔄 2.1.4 GENETIC vs EMPIRICAL CLASSIFICATION
notes:
🧬 Genetic :- focuses on the causes and processes producing climate.

📊 Empirical :- focuses mainly on measured climatic data and established boundaries.

⭐ Easy distinction :-
Genetic = Why does the climate occur?
Empirical = What climatic conditions are observed?

title: 🌍 2.2 KÖPPEN'S CLIMATE CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Köppen's system is one of the most widely used climate classification systems.

It is based mainly on :-
🌡️ Temperature
🌧️ Precipitation
🌿 Natural vegetation

Köppen recognized that vegetation responds strongly to temperature and moisture. Climatic boundaries were therefore related to vegetation zones.

📅 Initial classification :- 1900
🔄 Major revision :- 1940

⭐ Main strength :- simple, measurable and shows the relationship between climate and vegetation.

title: 🔤 2.2.1 FIVE MAJOR KÖPPEN CLIMATE TYPES
notes:
🌴 A :- Tropical climate
🏜️ B :- Dry climate
🌳 C :- Mid-latitude mild / Mesothermal climate
❄️ D :- Mid-latitude cold / Microthermal climate
🧊 E :- Polar climate

⭐ Temperature mainly controls A, C, D and E, while dryness is the dominant characteristic of B.

title: 🌴 2.2.2 TROPICAL CLIMATE (A)
notes:
Tropical climate :- every month has an average temperature above 18°C.

🔹 No true winter season.
🔹 Warm conditions throughout the year.
🔹 Mainly occurs in low latitudes.

Three important types :-
🌧️ Af :- Tropical wet / equatorial rainforest.
🌧️ Am :- Tropical monsoon.
🌦️ Aw :- Tropical wet and dry / savanna.

title: 🌧️ 2.2.3 TROPICAL WET (Af)
notes:
Af :- tropical rainforest climate.

🔹 Rainfall occurs throughout the year.
🔹 Very small monthly temperature variation.
🔹 High humidity and frequent convectional rainfall.
🔹 Dense, tall, broad-leaved evergreen rainforest vegetation.

🌎 Major areas :- Amazon Basin, Congo Basin and parts of Southeast Asia.

⭐ Af = tropical + wet all year.

title: 🌧️ 2.2.4 TROPICAL MONSOON (Am)
notes:
Am :- tropical climate with a strong seasonal concentration of rainfall.

🔹 Most rainfall occurs during the 7–9 hottest months.
🔹 Dry season receives very little rainfall.
🔹 Rainfall can be similar to or greater than Af annually.
🔹 Supports rainforest vegetation.

🌏 Examples :- parts of India and Southeast Asia.

⭐ Am = tropical + monsoon rainfall.

title: 🌦️ 2.2.5 TROPICAL WET AND DRY / SAVANNA (Aw)
notes:
Aw :- tropical climate with a prolonged dry season, especially during the winter season.

🔹 Distinct rainy and dry seasons.
🔹 Rainy season often has thunderstorms.
🔹 Dry season is strongly influenced by subtropical high pressure.
🔹 Savanna vegetation dominates.

🌍 Examples :- African savanna and tropical South America.

⭐ Aw = tropical + wet season + long dry season.

title: 🏜️ 2.2.6 DRY CLIMATE (B)
notes:
Dry climate :- precipitation is deficient for much of the year and evaporation often exceeds precipitation.

Two major groups :-
🏜️ BW :- Desert climate.
🌾 BS :- Semi-arid / Steppe climate.

Further divisions :-
🔥 h :- hot; mean annual temperature above 18°C.
❄️ k :- cold; mean annual temperature below 18°C.

Therefore :-
BWh :- hot desert
BWk :- cold desert
BSh :- hot steppe
BSk :- cold steppe.

title: 🏜️ 2.2.7 DESERT (BW) AND STEPPE (BS)
notes:
🏜️ BW Desert :- very dry climate with sparse xerophytic vegetation; occurs mainly around subtropical high-pressure belts and other dry environments.

🌾 BS Steppe :- semi-arid grassland climate with more precipitation than desert regions.

⭐ Important distinction :-
BW = true desert
BS = semi-arid steppe

title: 🌳 2.2.8 MID-LATITUDE MILD / MESOTHERMAL (C)
notes:
C climate :- average temperature of the coldest month is below 18°C but above -3°C.

🔹 Generally has mild winters and warmer summers.
🔹 Common in mid-latitude areas.
🔹 Seasonal precipitation patterns create different subgroups.

Major types discussed :-
🌧️ Cf :- wet throughout the year.
☀️ Cs :- dry summer.
❄️ Cw :- dry winter.

title: 🌧️ 2.2.9 MID-LATITUDE WET (Cf)
notes:
Cf :- precipitation occurs throughout the year.

Two important subdivisions :-
🌳 Cfa :- Humid subtropical; warm humid summers and frequent thunderstorms, mainly on eastern continental margins.
🌊 Cfb :- Marine west coast; humid conditions, short dry summer and persistent mid-latitude cyclones, mainly on western continental margins.

⭐ Cf = precipitation throughout the year.

title: ❄️ 2.2.10 MID-LATITUDE WINTER DRY (Cw / Dw)
notes:
Cw and Dw :- distinct seasonal temperature and precipitation patterns.

☀️ Summer :- generally hot and humid with showers and thunderstorms.

❄️ Winter :- colder and drier because continental polar air masses dominate.

🌾 Major vegetation :- grassland.

🌍 Mainly found in continental interiors of North America and Eurasia.

title: ☀️ 2.2.11 MID-LATITUDE SUMMER DRY (Cs)
notes:
Cs :- Mediterranean-type climate.

🔹 Dry, hot summers.
🔹 Mild, wetter winters.
🔹 Winter precipitation is associated with mid-latitude cyclones.
🔹 Summer dryness results from subtropical high-pressure subsidence.
🔹 Chaparral and sclerophyll vegetation are common.

🌍 Examples :- Mediterranean region, California, central Chile, Cape Town region and parts of southern Australia.

⭐ Cs = dry summer + wet winter.

title: ❄️ 2.2.12 MID-LATITUDE COLD / MICROTHERMAL (D)
notes:
D climate :- average temperature of the warmest month exceeds 10°C while the coldest monthly average is below -3°C.

🔹 Strong seasonal temperature differences.
🔹 Cold winters.
🔹 Warmer summers.
🔹 Mainly occurs in higher-latitude continental interiors.

⭐ D = cold mid-latitude climate.

title: 🧊 2.2.13 POLAR CLIMATE (E)
notes:
E climate :- average temperature of the warmest month is below 10°C.

🔹 Extremely cold conditions.
🔹 No true warm summer season.

Two major types :-
🌿 ET :- Polar tundra.
🧊 EF :- Polar ice cap.

⭐ E = very cold polar climate.

title: 🔢 2.2.14 KÖPPEN CLIMATE SYMBOLS
notes:
First-order groups :-
A :- Tropical
B :- Dry
C :- Mid-latitude mild
D :- Mid-latitude cold
E :- Polar

Second-order symbols :-
f :- wet throughout the year
m :- tropical monsoon
s :- dry summer
w :- dry winter
W :- true desert
S :- semi-arid / steppe
T :- tundra
F :- ice cap

Third-order symbols :-
a :- hot summer
b :- warm summer
c :- mild summer
d :- cool summer
h :- hot dry climate
k :- cold dry climate

⭐ Example :- Cfa = C + f + a = mid-latitude mild + wet throughout the year + hot summer.

title: 🔄 2.2.15 MODIFIED KÖPPEN-GEIGER CLASSIFICATION
notes:
Rudolf Geiger modified Köppen's system in 1961 to improve the relationship between climatic zones and biomes.

The modified system combines first-, second- and third-order classifications to describe climate more precisely.

⭐ More detailed symbols = more precise climatic description.

title: ⚖️ 2.2.16 MERITS AND LIMITATIONS OF KÖPPEN'S SYSTEM
notes:
✅ Merits :-
🔹 Simple and easy to apply.
🔹 Uses measurable temperature and precipitation data.
🔹 Clearly defines climatic boundaries.
🔹 Shows the relationship between climate and natural vegetation.
🔹 Useful for comparing climatic regions globally.

⚠️ Limitations :-
🔹 Does not adequately consider precipitation intensity.
🔹 Does not consider cloudiness and number of rainy days.
🔹 Does not adequately consider daily temperature extremes.
🔹 Gives little attention to winds and air masses.
🔹 Mountain and fog climates are not sufficiently represented.
🔹 Natural vegetation may respond slowly to environmental change.

title: 🌍 2.3 WORLD CLIMATIC REGIONS
notes:
World climatic regions are broadly grouped into :-

🌴 Low-latitude climates
🌳 Mid-latitude climates
❄️ High-latitude climates
🏔️ Highland climates

⭐ These broad groups are based mainly on Köppen classification and seasonal dominance of air masses.

title: 🌴 2.3.1 LOW-LATITUDE CLIMATIC REGIONS
notes:
Low-latitude regions include major tropical and subtropical climates.

Main types :-
1️⃣ Tropical wet
2️⃣ Tropical wet and dry
3️⃣ Dry desert and steppe

⭐ Common controls :- strong solar heating, ITCZ movement, tropical air masses and subtropical high pressure.

title: 🌧️ 2.3.2 TROPICAL WET REGION
notes:
🌍 Location :- around the Equator, approximately 6°N–6°S in the detailed world-region discussion.

🔹 High temperatures throughout the year.
🔹 Rainfall is abundant and well distributed.
🔹 Frequent convectional rainfall and thunderstorms.
🔹 Dense evergreen rainforest vegetation.

🌎 Examples :- Amazon Basin, Congo Basin, East Indies and areas from Sumatra to New Guinea.

⭐ Climate code :- Af.

title: 🌦️ 2.3.3 TROPICAL WET AND DRY REGION
notes:
🌍 Location :- approximately 6°–15° north and south latitudes.

🔹 Distinct wet and dry seasons.
🔹 ITCZ migration controls seasonal rainfall.
🔹 Rainy season occurs with high sun and convergence.
🔹 Dry season is associated with subtropical high-pressure subsidence.
🔹 Savanna vegetation dominates.

🌍 Examples :- India, Indochina, West Africa, southern Africa, South America and northern Australia.

title: 🏜️ 2.3.4 SUBTROPICAL DRY DESERT AND STEPPE
notes:
🌍 Location :- approximately 15°–25° north and south latitudes.

🔹 Dominated by continental tropical air masses.
🔹 High temperatures.
🔹 Very low and unreliable precipitation.
🔹 Low relative humidity and cloud cover.
🔹 Subtropical high-pressure subsidence produces stable, dry air.
🔹 Desert and steppe vegetation dominates.

🌎 Examples :- North Africa, southwestern USA, northern Mexico, southern Africa, Argentina and central Australia.

title: 🌳 2.3.5 MID-LATITUDE CLIMATIC REGIONS
notes:
Mid-latitude climates are mainly influenced by the interaction between tropical air masses moving poleward and polar air masses moving toward the Equator.

Main types :-
🏜️ Mid-latitude desert and steppe
🌳 Mid-latitude wet
❄️ Mid-latitude winter dry
☀️ Mid-latitude summer dry

title: 🏜️ 2.3.6 MID-LATITUDE DESERT AND STEPPE
notes:
🌍 Location :- approximately 30°–55° north and south latitudes.

🔹 Summers are influenced by continental tropical air masses.
🔹 Winters are influenced by continental polar air masses.
🔹 Low precipitation and humidity.
🔹 Larger annual and daily temperature ranges than subtropical deserts.
🔹 Rain-shadow effects can reduce moisture.

🌎 Examples :- areas east of the Caspian Sea, north of the Himalayas, western USA and east of the Andes.

⭐ Steppe receives more precipitation than desert.

title: 🌳 2.3.7 MID-LATITUDE WET REGION
notes:
🔹 Influenced by maritime tropical air masses during summer.
🔹 Mid-latitude cyclones influence winter weather.
🔹 Precipitation is abundant and generally distributed throughout the year.
🔹 Deciduous forests are important vegetation.

🌎 Examples :- eastern parts of North America, southeastern South America, New Zealand and southeastern Australia.

title: ☀️ 2.3.8 MID-LATITUDE WINTER DRY REGION
notes:
🔹 Hot and humid summers.
🔹 Cold and dry winters.
🔹 Summer thunderstorms and showers are common.
🔹 Continental polar air dominates winter.
🔹 Grassland is a major vegetation type.

🌎 Mainly found in interior regions of North America and Eurasia.

title: 🌞 2.3.9 MID-LATITUDE SUMMER DRY / MEDITERRANEAN REGION
notes:
🔹 Located mainly on western continental margins between about 30° and 50° latitude.
🔹 Hot and dry summers.
🔹 Mild and wet winters.
🔹 Winter rainfall comes mainly from mid-latitude cyclones.
🔹 Summer dryness results from subtropical high-pressure subsidence.
🔹 Chaparral and sclerophyll vegetation dominate.

🌍 Examples :- Mediterranean Basin, California, central Chile, Cape Town region and southern Australia.

title: ❄️ 2.3.10 HIGH-LATITUDE CLIMATIC REGIONS
notes:
High-latitude climates occur toward the polar regions.

Main types :-
🌿 Polar tundra (ET)
🧊 Polar ice cap (EF)

⭐ General characteristics :- very low temperatures, long cold winters and limited vegetation.

title: 🌿 2.3.11 POLAR TUNDRA (ET)
notes:
Polar tundra :- cold winters and cool summers with a summer rainfall regime.

🔹 Warmest conditions occur during the short summer.
🔹 Annual precipitation is generally low.
🔹 Vegetation includes mosses, lichens, dwarf trees and scattered shrubs.

🌎 Examples :- Arctic coasts, Iceland, coastal Greenland and parts of northern Eurasia.

title: 🧊 2.3.12 POLAR ICE CAP (EF)
notes:
Polar ice cap :- extremely cold climate where the land surface remains permanently covered by snow and ice.

🔹 Warmest-month average is about 0°C or below.
🔹 Very limited or no natural vegetation.
🔹 Covers large areas of Greenland and Antarctica.
🔹 Strong and persistent winds can produce blizzard conditions.

⭐ EF = permanent ice and extreme cold.

title: 🏔️ 2.3.13 HIGHLAND CLIMATE
notes:
Highland climate :- climate strongly influenced by elevation and mountain topography.

🔹 Temperature decreases as elevation increases.
🔹 Precipitation can increase because of orographic lifting.
🔹 Climate can change greatly over short horizontal distances.
🔹 Slope orientation affects solar radiation and temperature.
🔹 Mountains create barriers that influence wind and precipitation.

🌍 Highland climates occur in mountains and high plateaus at many latitudes.

⭐ Elevation can create cold or tundra-like conditions even in low latitudes.

title: 🌡️ 2.4 FACTORS INFLUENCING WORLD CLIMATIC REGIONS
notes:
Major climate controls include :-

1️⃣ Latitude / seasonality
2️⃣ Earth's revolution, rotation and axial tilt
3️⃣ Continentality and distribution of land and water
4️⃣ Atmospheric circulation
5️⃣ Seasonal movement of subtropical high pressure
6️⃣ Coriolis effect
7️⃣ Ocean circulation
8️⃣ Elevation / topography

⭐ These factors work together to produce the world's climatic patterns.

title: ☀️ 2.4.1 LATITUDE / SEASONALITY
notes:
Latitude strongly affects the amount and angle of incoming solar energy.

🌍 Low latitudes :-
🔹 Sun's rays are more direct.
🔹 Greater heating.
🔹 Smaller seasonal temperature changes.

❄️ High latitudes :-
🔹 Sun's rays strike at lower angles.
🔹 Solar energy is spread over a larger area.
🔹 Greater seasonal differences.
🔹 Winters are much colder.

⭐ Latitude is one of the fundamental controls of global temperature distribution.

title: 🌍 2.4.2 REVOLUTION, ROTATION AND EARTH'S TILT
notes:
Earth's revolution around the Sun, rotation and axial tilt influence the distribution of solar energy.

🔹 Axial tilt changes the angle of sunlight during the year.
🔹 Revolution produces seasonal changes.
🔹 Day length changes with latitude and season.
🔹 Low latitudes receive relatively consistent solar energy.
🔹 High latitudes experience large seasonal differences in daylight and solar heating.

⭐ Combined effect = seasonal variation in climate.

title: 🌊 2.4.3 CONTINENTALITY / LAND AND WATER
notes:
Land and water heat and cool at different rates.

🌊 Maritime influence :- water moderates temperature and supplies moisture.

🌍 Continentality :- interiors of large continents experience greater temperature extremes because they are far from the moderating influence of oceans.

🔹 Coastal areas generally have smaller temperature ranges.
🔹 Continental interiors generally have larger temperature ranges.

⭐ Same latitude does not always mean the same climate.

title: 🌬️ 2.4.4 ATMOSPHERIC CIRCULATION
notes:
Atmospheric circulation redistributes heat and moisture across Earth.

🔹 Air moves from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure areas.
🔹 Rising air in low-pressure zones promotes cloud formation and precipitation.
🔹 Sinking air in high-pressure zones generally produces stable and dry conditions.

⭐ Main role :- balance unequal heating between different latitudes.

title: 🔄 2.4.5 SEASONAL MOVEMENT OF SUBTROPICAL HIGH PRESSURE
notes:
Subtropical high-pressure belts occur around 30° latitude and shift seasonally.

🔹 Their movement affects surface winds and rainfall patterns.
🔹 ITCZ is associated with low pressure, rising air, clouds and precipitation.
🔹 Subtropical high pressure is associated with sinking, stable and often dry air.

⭐ Seasonal movement of these pressure belts helps explain wet and dry seasons in many tropical and subtropical regions.

title: 🌀 2.4.6 CORIOLIS EFFECT, CENTRIFUGAL FORCE & FRICTION
notes:
🌀 Coriolis effect :- apparent deflection of moving air and other objects caused by Earth's rotation.

🔄 Centrifugal acceleration :- apparent outward-directed effect associated with movement along a curved path.

🪨 Friction :- resistance between moving air and Earth's surface.

🔹 Friction is strongest near the surface.
🔹 Mountains create greater surface friction than smooth ocean surfaces.

⭐ These factors influence wind direction and speed.

title: 🌊 2.4.7 OCEAN CIRCULATION
notes:
Ocean circulation redistributes heat across Earth's surface.

🔹 Surface currents are strongly influenced by winds and pressure systems.
🔹 Warm currents transfer heat toward cooler regions.
🔹 Cold currents transfer cooler water toward warmer regions.
🔹 Ocean currents influence coastal temperature and precipitation.

⭐ Oceans act as major regulators of global climate.

title: 🏔️ 2.4.8 TOPOGRAPHY / ELEVATION
notes:
Elevation strongly affects temperature and precipitation.

🌡️ Normal lapse rate :- temperature decreases by about 6.4°C for every 1 km increase in elevation in the lower atmosphere.

🔹 Higher elevations = lower temperatures.
🔹 Mountain slopes receive different amounts of solar radiation depending on orientation.
🔹 Mountains can force moist air upward, producing orographic rainfall.
🔹 Leeward sides can experience rain-shadow conditions.

⭐ Example from the textbook :- At 4,620 m, using a 6.4°C/km lapse rate and 30°C sea-level temperature, the estimated temperature is about 0.43°C.

title: 🌧️ 2.4.9 OROGRAPHIC RAINFALL
notes:
Orographic rainfall :- precipitation produced when moist air is forced upward by mountains.

🌬️ Windward side :-
🔹 Air rises.
🔹 Air cools and condenses.
🔹 More precipitation occurs.

🏜️ Leeward side :-
🔹 Air descends.
🔹 It becomes warmer and drier.
🔹 Rain-shadow conditions may develop.

⭐ Mountains can therefore create different climates on opposite sides.

title: 🇪🇹 2.5 LOCAL / INDIGENOUS CLIMATE CLASSIFICATION OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Ethiopia's traditional climate classification is based mainly on :-
🏔️ Height / elevation
🌡️ Temperature
🌱 Length of growing season

Five primary climatic zones :-
1️⃣ Bereha
2️⃣ Kolla
3️⃣ Woina-Dega
4️⃣ Dega
5️⃣ Wurch

⭐ Ethiopian classification strongly emphasizes altitude and its effect on temperature and agricultural conditions.

title: 🔥 2.5.1 BEREHA
notes:
Bereha :- hot, desert-like lowland climate.

📍 Elevation :- below 500 m above sea level.
🌡️ Average annual temperature :- above 30°C.
🌧️ Average annual rainfall :- less than 16 inches.

🔹 Very hot conditions.
🔹 Strong winds.
🔹 Low relative humidity.
🔹 Limited cloud cover.
🔹 Harsh environment.
🔹 Pastoralism is common.

📍 Examples :- Afar lowlands and Somali lowlands.

title: 🌵 2.5.2 KOLLA
notes:
Kolla :- warm to hot, semi-arid lowland climate.

📍 Elevation :- 500–1,500 m.
🌡️ Average annual temperature :- 20–30°C.
🌧️ Average annual rainfall :- about 16.4–32.8 inches.

🔹 Rainfall varies considerably from year to year.
🔹 Western Gambella lowlands can receive much higher rainfall.
🔹 Climate may be hot and humid in wetter areas.

🌾 Common crops :- sorghum, finger millet, groundnuts, cowpeas and sesame.

title: 🌾 2.5.3 WOINA-DEGA
notes:
Woina-Dega :- temperate highland climate.

📍 Elevation :- 1,500–2,300 m.
🌡️ Average annual temperature :- 15–20°C.
🌧️ Average annual rainfall :- about 48 inches.

🌾 Common crops :-
🔹 Wheat
🔹 Teff
🔹 Barley
🔹 Maize
🔹 Sorghum
🔹 Chickpeas
🔹 Haricot beans

⭐ Woina-Dega is an important agricultural climatic zone.

title: 🌤️ 2.5.4 DEGA
notes:
Dega :- cold temperate highland climate.

📍 Elevation :- 2,300–3,300 m.
🌡️ Coldest month :- below 10°C.
🌧️ Annual rainfall :- about 40–80 inches.

🌾 Common crops :-
🔹 Wheat
🔹 Highland pulses
🔹 Highland oilseeds

⭐ Increasing elevation produces cooler conditions than Woina-Dega.

title: 🏔️ 2.5.5 WURCH
notes:
Wurch :- alpine climate found at very high elevations.

📍 Elevation :- above 3,300 m.
🌡️ Average annual temperature :- below 10°C.
🌧️ Annual rainfall :- about 35.2–80 inches.

📍 Examples :-
🔹 Afro-alpine plateaus / Senate plateaus
🔹 Simien Mountains / Ras Dejen
🔹 Guna Mountains
🔹 Choke Mountains
🔹 Amare Saint in South Wollo

🌾 Barley is commonly produced.

⭐ Wurch = highest + coldest major traditional climatic zone.

title: 📊 2.5.6 ETHIOPIAN CLIMATE ZONES AT A GLANCE
notes:
🔥 Bereha :- <500 m | >30°C | <16 in rainfall | hot desert-like lowland

🌵 Kolla :- 500–1,500 m | 20–30°C | 16.4–32.8 in | warm/hot semi-arid

🌾 Woina-Dega :- 1,500–2,300 m | 15–20°C | ~48 in | temperate highland

🌤️ Dega :- 2,300–3,300 m | coldest month <10°C | 40–80 in | cold highland

🏔️ Wurch :- >3,300 m | <10°C | 35.2–80 in | alpine

⭐ General pattern :- As elevation increases, temperature generally decreases.

title: ⚖️ 2.5.7 LOCAL vs KÖPPEN CLASSIFICATION
notes:
🇪🇹 Local Ethiopian classification :-
🔹 Mainly based on elevation, temperature and growing-season length.
🔹 Closely connected with traditional agroecological conditions.
🔹 Uses names such as Bereha, Kolla, Woina-Dega, Dega and Wurch.

🌍 Köppen classification :-
🔹 Mainly uses temperature, precipitation and vegetation relationships.
🔹 Uses symbols such as A, B, C, D, E, Af, Am, Aw, BWh and Cfa.
🔹 Designed for broad global climate classification.

⭐ Key difference :- Local classification emphasizes altitude and agricultural conditions, while Köppen emphasizes measurable temperature, precipitation and vegetation relationships.

title: 🌱 2.5.8 CLIMATE AND AGRICULTURE IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
Climate zones influence the types of crops that can grow successfully.

🔥 Hot lowlands :- pastoralism and drought-tolerant crops are important.

🌾 Kolla :- sorghum, finger millet, groundnuts, cowpeas and sesame.

🌾 Woina-Dega :- wheat, teff, barley, maize, sorghum, chickpeas and haricot beans.

🌾 Dega :- wheat, highland pulses and highland oilseeds.

🏔️ Wurch :- barley is commonly produced.

⭐ Elevation changes temperature and growing conditions, which influences agricultural patterns.

title: 🧠 UNIT 2 KEY CONCEPTS
notes:
🌡️ Climate classification :- grouping places according to climatic similarities.

🧬 Genetic classification :- based on processes causing climate.

📊 Empirical classification :- based on observed climatic data.

🌍 Köppen :- major global empirical classification system.

🌴 A :- Tropical
🏜️ B :- Dry
🌳 C :- Mid-latitude mild
❄️ D :- Mid-latitude cold
🧊 E :- Polar

🌧️ Af :- Tropical wet
🌧️ Am :- Tropical monsoon
🌦️ Aw :- Tropical wet and dry / savanna
🏜️ BW :- Desert
🌾 BS :- Steppe

🌍 World climate groups :- Low-latitude + Mid-latitude + High-latitude + Highland.

☀️ Major climate controls :- Latitude + Earth's movements + Continentality + Atmospheric circulation + Subtropical high pressure + Coriolis effect + Ocean circulation + Elevation.

🇪🇹 Ethiopian zones :- Bereha + Kolla + Woina-Dega + Dega + Wurch.

title: ⭐ UNIT 2 QUICK REVISION
notes:
📌 Climate classification simplifies global climatic diversity.

📌 Ancient Greeks used the Torrid, Temperate and Frigid zones.

📌 Genetic classification focuses on causes; empirical classification focuses on observed data.

📌 Köppen uses mainly temperature, precipitation and vegetation relationships.

📌 Five major Köppen groups :- A, B, C, D and E.

📌 A :- Tropical; B :- Dry; C :- Mid-latitude mild; D :- Mid-latitude cold; E :- Polar.

📌 Tropical subtypes :- Af, Am and Aw.

📌 Dry subtypes :- BW and BS; h = hot, k = cold.

📌 World regions :- Low-latitude, Mid-latitude, High-latitude and Highland.

📌 Latitude affects solar heating and seasonality.

📌 Land and water heat at different rates, producing maritime and continental effects.

📌 Atmospheric circulation redistributes heat and moisture.

📌 Ocean currents transfer heat and influence coastal climates.

📌 Temperature normally decreases about 6.4°C per km of elevation in the lower atmosphere.

📌 Mountains can produce orographic rainfall and rain-shadow effects.

📌 Ethiopia's traditional climate classification uses elevation, temperature and growing season.

📌 Ethiopian zones from lowest to highest :- Bereha → Kolla → Woina-Dega → Dega → Wurch.

⭐ Core idea :- Climate is controlled by several interacting physical factors, and classification systems help organize the world's climatic diversity.
